arguments.title: Split the expense-report god module into a pipeline
arguments.spec:
# Refactor: Split the Expense-Report God Module Into a Pipeline

`src/reporting.mjs` turns lines of text into an expense report. It works. It is one function doing five jobs
(parsing, validating, aggregating, formatting, exporting), and its money formatter has a verbatim twin in
`src/receipts.mjs`. Split it into stages; change nothing it produces. `src/index.mjs` must keep exporting
`buildReport`, `exportReportCsv`, `CATEGORIES` and `renderReceipt` by those exact names.

The behaviour, stated precisely (frozen scenarios own these, read them before touching anything):
- Input is one record per line, `category,who,amount`, surrounding whitespace trimmed. A blank line or one
  starting with `#` is skipped, not rejected.
- Rejection rules, in this reporting order: wrong field count -> `expected three fields`; category not in
  `CATEGORIES` -> `unknown category <name>`; empty owner -> `missing owner`; amount not matching an optional
  sign, digits and at most two decimals -> `bad amount <text>`; a negative amount without `allowRefunds` ->
  `refunds are not allowed`. Each rejection carries a 1-based line number.
- Amounts are held in minor units. `options` is optional in every form (absent, undefined, `{}`).
- Aggregates come back in `CATEGORIES` order, each with `totalMinor`, `count`, sorted unique `owners`, and
  `averageMinor` rounded to the nearest minor unit.
- The table pads each label to the width of the longest name in `CATEGORIES`, then two spaces, the amount
  right-aligned in 10, two spaces, the count right-aligned in 3. A `TOTAL` row always follows, counting accepted
  rows.
- The CSV export has a `category,total,count,owners` header and space-joined owners.
- A receipt is category padded to 8, owner padded to 12, amount right-aligned in 10; a missing category throws
  `TypeError`.

`scenarios/`, `test/refactor.test.js` and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are FROZEN evidence, digest-checked on every
run. Two things are measured every run: BEHAVIOUR (all 9 frozen scenarios B01-B09 must keep passing exactly as
before) and STRUCTURE, graded against exactly four goals in `refactor/manifest.json`'s `refactor/goals.json`:

- G1 `max_module_lines` (limit 40) -- verified against the real fixture: the unmodified `src/reporting.mjs` is
  77 meaningful lines.
- G2 `max_function_lines` (limit 20) -- verified against the real fixture: the unmodified `buildReport` is 61
  meaningful lines.
- G3 `max_branches_per_function` (limit 5, counted as if/case/ternary/&&/||/catch) -- verified against the real
  fixture: the unmodified `buildReport` has 15 branch points.
- G4 `no_duplicate_block` (windowLines 5) -- verified against the real fixture: the unmodified tree fails this
  now (`formatMoneyMinor` is byte-identical in `src/reporting.mjs` and `src/receipts.mjs`).

The deliverable is `refactor/manifest.json`: `addressed` lists the goal ids genuinely met; every goal listed is
checked immediately and strictly. `complete: true` requires every goal listed and met. `npm test` must pass
exactly as-is, offline -- never add a dependency.

One repair, hand-verified against the real fixture in a scratch copy to satisfy all four goals at once while
leaving all 9 frozen behaviour scenarios passing unchanged (14/14 total, including with `complete: true`):
split the single god-function into a small pipeline of single-purpose modules, and give the five rejection
rules a one-rule-per-function shape instead of a five-branch-deep conditional chain. Extract: `src/categories.mjs`
(`CATEGORIES`, unchanged), `src/money.mjs` (`formatMoneyMinor`, unchanged -- the one place it lives now, which is
what removes the G4 duplication), `src/amount.mjs` (`isValidAmountText` and `amountMinorOf`, split out of the
amount-text handling), `src/rejectionRules.mjs` (the five rejection rules as five tiny named functions in an
ordered list, walked by one small generic `rejectionFor` engine -- a direct transcription of the five checks in
their existing order, not a redesign), `src/parsing.mjs` (`splitFields` and `parseLine`, composing the above),
`src/aggregate.mjs` (`aggregateRows`, the existing grouping/averaging, moved unchanged), `src/table.mjs`
(`renderTable`, the existing padding/table-line logic, moved unchanged). `src/reporting.mjs` shrinks to
`buildReport` (the line loop, now calling `parseLine` per line) and `exportReportCsv` (unchanged body, now using
the shared `formatMoneyMinor`). `src/receipts.mjs` keeps `renderReceipt` unchanged except importing
`formatMoneyMinor` from `src/money.mjs` instead of carrying its own copy. `src/index.mjs` keeps exporting all
four names, from whichever files now hold them.
arguments.plan:
Two cards, chained:

1. `split-reporting-pipeline-and-shared-money-format` -- does the actual restructuring: seven new/changed
   support modules (src/categories.mjs, src/money.mjs, src/amount.mjs, src/rejectionRules.mjs, src/parsing.mjs,
   src/aggregate.mjs, src/table.mjs), plus src/reporting.mjs shrunk to a thin pipeline, src/receipts.mjs sharing
   the money formatter, and src/index.mjs re-exporting the same four names. Verified empirically against the
   real fixture: all 9 behaviour scenarios (B01-B09) still pass, and claiming G1+G2+G3+G4 against the refactored
   tree is genuinely accepted by the real frozen verifier (worst module 31/40 lines, worst function 16/20 lines,
   worst branch count 4/5). This card lists all four goals in refactor/manifest.json's `addressed` (leaving
   `complete: false`) once it has verified them itself via a real npm test run in-session.
2. `verify-and-complete-expense-report-refactor` (depends on 1) -- independently re-verifies (does not trust the
   previous card) that all four goals are genuinely met via a fresh npm test run, then sets `complete: true`.

tasks.prompt:
Restructure src/ so buildReport stops being one function doing five jobs, and the money
formatter stops being duplicated between reporting.mjs and receipts.mjs.

Baseline (verified against the real fixture, not assumed): claiming G1+G2+G3+G4 against the UNMODIFIED tree
fails all four -- src/reporting.mjs is 77 meaningful lines (limit 40), buildReport is 61 meaningful lines (limit
20) with 15 branch points (limit 5), and formatMoneyMinor is byte-identical in src/reporting.mjs and
src/receipts.mjs.

Read the behaviour section of specification.md and scenarios/reporting.scenarios.mjs (B01-B09) before writing
anything -- the rejection order, minor-unit rounding and column widths are all observable and must be reproduced
exactly, not re-derived from what the current code looks like it does.

Shape (verified empirically against the real fixture: all 9 frozen behaviour scenarios B01-B09 keep passing
exactly as before, and G1+G2+G3+G4 are all genuinely accepted by the real frozen verifier, including with
`complete: true`):

- New `src/categories.mjs` exporting `CATEGORIES` (the existing array, moved here UNCHANGED).
- New `src/money.mjs` exporting `formatMoneyMinor(amountMinor)` (the existing function, moved here UNCHANGED).
  This is the ONE place the money-formatting rule lives now -- both reporting and receipts call it, which is
  what makes G4 pass.
- New `src/amount.mjs` exporting `isValidAmountText(amountText)` (wraps the existing `^-?\d+(?:\.\d{1,2})?$`
  pattern test) and `amountMinorOf(amountText)` (the existing `Math.round(Number(amountText) * 100)`).
- New `src/rejectionRules.mjs` exporting `rejectionFor(parts, options)`. Internally, five small named functions
  -- one per existing rejection check, in the SAME order (field count, category, owner, amount format, refund)
  -- each returning either a reason string or null, held in an ordered list that `rejectionFor` walks, returning
  the first non-null reason or null if every rule passes. Every reason string must come out byte-identical to
  today.
- New `src/parsing.mjs` exporting `splitFields(raw)` (the existing comma-split-and-trim, moved UNCHANGED) and
  `parseLine(raw, options)`: splits the fields, calls `rejectionFor`; if it returns a reason, return
  `{ ok: false, reason }`; otherwise return `{ ok: true, row: { category, who, amountMinor } }` using
  `amountMinorOf` for the amount.
- New `src/aggregate.mjs` exporting `aggregateRows(rows)` -- the existing byCategory Map grouping, filtered and
  mapped into CATEGORIES order with sorted unique owners and a rounded average, moved here UNCHANGED.
- New `src/table.mjs` exporting `renderTable(aggregates, totalMinor, acceptedCount)` -- the existing
  padding/table-line logic (pad to the widest CATEGORIES name, amount right-aligned in 10, count right-aligned
  in 3, trailing TOTAL row over `acceptedCount`), moved here UNCHANGED, using `formatMoneyMinor` from
  src/money.mjs.
- `src/reporting.mjs`: shrinks to `buildReport` (loops the input lines, skips blank/`#` lines, calls `parseLine`
  per remaining line, collects `rows`/`rejected`, then calls `aggregateRows` and `renderTable`) and
  `exportReportCsv` (unchanged body, using the shared `formatMoneyMinor`).
- `src/receipts.mjs`: `renderReceipt` unchanged, importing `formatMoneyMinor` from `src/money.mjs` instead of
  keeping its own copy.
- `src/index.mjs`: keep exporting `buildReport`, `exportReportCsv`, `CATEGORIES` and `renderReceipt` by those
  exact names (the file each comes from may change).

Do not change any rejection reason, rejection order, column width, or rounding rule. Never add a dependency (the
sandbox is offline).

Steps: (1) read_files src/index.mjs, src/reporting.mjs, src/receipts.mjs, scenarios/reporting.scenarios.mjs
fresh. (2) In a later turn, write the seven new modules and rewrite reporting.mjs, receipts.mjs and index.mjs
(write_file for whole-file rewrites; do not retry an identical rejected edit_file call more than once -- fall
back to write_file). (3) In a further later turn, run npm test and confirm every one of the 9 behaviour
scenarios (B01-B09) still passes -- the manifest is still empty at this point, so the goal checks stay
trivially green regardless; behaviour is what this run actually proves. (4) In a further later turn, read
refactor/manifest.json fresh and edit it to set `addressed` to `["G1", "G2", "G3", "G4"]`, leaving
`complete: false` -- the completeness flip belongs to the card that depends on this one. Re-read to confirm,
then run npm test once more (never in the same turn as the edit): the real frozen verifier now checks all four
goals for real, and ALL must be reported as met. If any fails, the failure message names the exact offending
module or function -- fix that specific thing and re-verify; never leave a goal listed that the verifier does
not confirm.

Turn discipline: never edit and verify in the same turn. Re-read a file immediately before writing an edit
